_basis.what_moves: The owner-run Global Scouter bundle contributes 1,082 canonical payload files and 87,268,011 bytes. The four derived core projections are excluded from this family and remain owned by their own publication path.
_basis.publication_cadence: The source declares weekly cadence. Five weekly generations are used for the conservative 30-day review envelope; this is a planning value, not a remote publication receipt.
_basis.r2_generation_model: One family publication contains 1,082 payload assets plus one immutable generation manifest. The all-changed ceiling therefore plans 1,083 puts per generation and 1,082 newly unreferenced payload objects at each rotation; manifests are never deletion candidates.
_basis.r2_retention_model: The family retains current, previous, and in_progress generations. The calculator carries those three measured slots independently. A five-sweep monthly review lists the 1,082 payload assets plus accumulated manifests in two 1,000-key pages per sweep, for 10 list operations; delete remains free and is recorded only as the all-changed rotation ceiling.
_basis.r2_class_b_model: The request demand carries a 500,000-operation serving planning ceiling plus 16,250 publication reads (1,083 presence reads + 1,083 readbacks + 1,083 parity reads + 1 resume check, times five generations) and 25 manifest-retention reads (five manifests reviewed across five sweeps). The account baseline is still required before this additive request plan can be called complete.
_basis.d1_model: One publication-generation row is added per weekly family generation, with the existing coordinator shape represented as a single table contract. The row, query, and purge values are explicit planning inputs and are not an account measurement.
_basis.kv_model: KV holds one active generation pointer. It is a cache and not publication authority; the single-pointer contract is retained in the demand so a multi-pointer plan fails closed.

_retention.rule_source: the shipped three-slot family retention contract
_retention.retained_set: current, previous, and in_progress for this family; prepared generations remain protected until their lifecycle resolves
_retention.delete_candidates: only unreferenced objects/sha256 payloads; generation manifests, pointers, probes, and protected evidence are never deletion candidates
_retention.overwrite_behaviour: zero. Content-addressed payload keys are reused when an unchanged asset is published
_retention.failed_generation_cleanup: an abandoned generation contributes only unreferenced payload keys to the ordinary retention sweep; no separate delete class is invented
_retention.fail_closed: an unreadable or missing retained manifest aborts the bucket-level sweep with zero deletions
_retention.worst_case_derivation: 1,082 payload deletes per all-changed weekly rotation times five planned generations equals 5,410 free DeleteObject operations per 30-day review
_retention.scope_caveat: retention is bucket-level in the publisher; these figures are this family's attributable planning envelope, not an independently schedulable remote operation
